newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds slip in moribund trade,no change seen.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds slip in moribund trade,no change seen.

text.p: Danish bond prices slipped undramatically on Monday in quiet trade with dealers looking to the U.S. opening to bring life back into a moribund market but expecting little change ahead.
"Unless the U.S. market moves when it opens later in the afternoon, I cannot see anything much happening here," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.07 point from the opening at 111.17, yielding 6.33 percent in turnover of only 850 million crowns while its March future rose 0.02 point to 111.12 with 196 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.25 point to 89.10.
The crown traded at 3.8120 per mark at 1150 gmt, up a tad from around 3.8123 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one basis point to 66 during the course of the morning.
